title: Refresh Terraform modules CI/CD pipeline and integration tests
author: Sahana Iyer
description: Context: Our Confluence CI/CD page for redwood-terraform describes the original alpha pipeline. Since then we’ve added more modules/examples and the integration suite has been flakier and harder to reason about (provider init duplication, inconsistent path filtering, unclear when to run AWS ephemeral tests). This PR refreshes the GitHub Actions workflows and updates the repo’s CI guidance to reflect the current reality. Summary of changes: (1) PR validation now uses a single module/example discovery step that drives a matrix for fmt/validate/tflint and avoids re-running init unnecessarily. (2) Security scanning: keep Checkov as the baseline gate but also upload Trivy IaC (config) results to SARIF for additional signal; Checkov remains the merge-blocking policy for now. (3) Integration tests: previously nightly + manual; now we also auto-run integration tests on PRs when risk classifier flags high-risk changes (NAT/routing, endpoints/DNS, IAM boundaries, SG egress posture). Low/medium risk PRs remain PR-fast by default. (4) AWS auth for integration tests migrated to aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4 with tighter session policies and explicit region allowlist; still OIDC, no long-lived keys. (5) Release workflow tightened: requires the latest integration run on main within the last 24h OR a release-triggered integration run attached to the release commit; adds a job summary section that captures Terraform + provider versions used for the release. Details (aligns with existing doc): Purpose: CI/CD pipeline for redwood-terraform modules. Goals: consistent fmt/validate/lint/security scanning; catch breaking networking/IAM changes early; predictable SemVer releases for pilot pinning. Non-goals unchanged: not deploying Redwood Private, AWS only, no long-lived envs. Required checks (PR): terraform fmt -check -recursive; terraform validate per changed module/example with plugin cache; tflint with AWS ruleset; checkov against modules/ + examples/ (SARIF upload); docs/examples sanity (validate canonical examples + README drift check); provider/version pin enforcement (Terraform matches .terraform-version; providers pinned; fail on new unpinned providers). Approval policy unchanged in spirit: min 2 approvals; Security Eng required for IAM/logging/egress/endpoint-policy changes; CODEOWNERS paths updated to include new modules/iam-boundaries and modules/vpc-endpoints. Integration tests (ephemeral AWS): still provision/assert/destroy in CI sandbox account, but now triggered by risk classifier for high-risk PRs + nightly + manual + release. Guardrails: SCP region allowlist; deny public S3; budget alarms. Cost controls: workflow timeout; smaller footprints; prefer endpoints over NAT where possible. Troubleshooting notes updated: most common failures now are endpoint eventual consistency and IAM propagation; we added retries to specific asserts and ensured destroy runs even after assert failures. This PR intentionally does not remove Checkov or change the exception policy semantics; it adds Trivy as a non-blocking signal and consolidates workflow structure for speed and clarity.
commits: ci: consolidate terraform init/validate into discovery-driven matrix
ci: add risk classifier for integration test auto-trigger on PRs
ci: add Trivy IaC SARIF upload (non-blocking) alongside Checkov
ci: migrate AWS OIDC config to configure-aws-credentials@v4 with tighter session policy
release: require recent green integration run and include version summary in job output
docs: update CI/CD guidance and CODEOWNERS notes for new module paths
ci_checks: pr / trivy iac (non-blocking) + SARIF upload: pass
integration / ephemeral-aws (auto-triggered by risk classifier): pass
review_thread: Victor Alvarez (review): Risk classifier: please ensure endpoint/DNS changes and NAT/route-table changes are both flagged. We’ve had PRs that only touch modules/endpoints but still break private DNS behavior. Also confirm integration tests still default to us-east-2 only. Sahana Iyer (author): Updated classifier to include modules/endpoints*, modules/vpc*, and any change under examples/networking*. Region remains us-east-2 only; denylist/allowlist enforced via env + SCP. Marcus Lin (review): Checkov exceptions: can you confirm we still require justification + scoped skip IDs, and that IAM boundary changes still require Security approval? Also don’t want Trivy to become blocking yet. Sahana Iyer (author): Confirmed. Checkov remains merge-blocking; Trivy is informational (continue-on-error) but uploads SARIF. CODEOWNERS updated to add modules/iam-boundaries/* under Security Eng. Connor O'Brien (review): Release gating: requiring a green integration run within 24h is good. Please document the fallback path (release-triggered integration attached to the commit) and ensure the workflow links the run URL in the release job summary. Sahana Iyer (author): Added fallback logic + job summary link to the integration run and the Terraform/provider versions used. Irene Choi (review): Workflow runtime: did the matrix consolidation actually reduce time? Sahana Iyer (author): Yes; PR checks went from ~14-18 min to ~9-11 min on typical module-only changes by avoiding repeated init and by path-filtering unchanged targets. Approvals: Victor Alvarez approved. Marcus Lin approved with note to revisit making Trivy blocking after we tune findings. Connor O'Brien approved. Merge: Squash merged by Sahana Iyer on 2025-09-10.
release_notes: CI/CD: PR checks now run via discovery-driven matrix for faster validation; integration tests auto-run on high-risk PRs (networking/endpoints/IAM boundary/SG egress) in addition to nightly/manual/release; security scanning keeps Checkov as blocking and adds Trivy IaC as non-blocking SARIF signal; release workflow now requires a recent green integration run and includes Terraform/provider version summary.
